Background

In the data folder, you will find data about shark incidents in California between 1950-2022. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

Load the libraries

library("tidyverse")
library("janitor")

Load the data

Run the following code chunk to import the data. In this chunk, I am removing NA’s.

sharks <- 
  read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv", 
           na=c("NA", "N/A", "Unknown", "NOT COUNTED", "", " ")) %>% 
  clean_names()

Questions

  1. Are there any “hotspots” for shark incidents in California? Show the top five counties with the most incidents.
sharks %>%
  count(county, sort= TRUE)
## # A tibble: 22 × 2
##    county              n
##    <chr>           <int>
##  1 San Diego          25
##  2 Humboldt           20
##  3 San Mateo          19
##  4 Santa Barbara      19
##  5 Marin              16
##  6 Monterey           16
##  7 Santa Cruz         15
##  8 Sonoma             15
##  9 San Luis Obispo    14
## 10 Los Angeles        10
## # ℹ 12 more rows
  1. Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents per county.
sharks %>%
  count(county) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= reorder(county, n), y= n)) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill=n)) + 
  coord_flip() +
  labs( 
    title= "Total number of Shark Incidents per county", x= "County", y= "Number of Incidents")

  1. Are there months of the year when incidents are more likely to occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by month. Which month has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  count(month, sort= TRUE) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= reorder(month,n), y= n)) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill = n)) + 
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title= "Number of Sharks Incidents by Month", x= "Month", y= "Number of Incidents"
  )

  1. Is there a time of day when most attacks occur? Make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by time of day. Which time of day has the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(time)) %>%
  count(time) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x=reorder(time,n), y=n), na.rm= TRUE) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill=time)) + 
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Total number of Incidents by time of day", x=" Time of Day", y= "Number of Incidents"
  )
## Warning in fortify(data, ...): Arguments in `...` must be used.
## ✖ Problematic argument:
## • na.rm = TRUE
## ℹ Did you misspell an argument name?

  1. How do the number and types of injuries compare by county? Make a table that shows the number of injury types by county. Which county has the highest number incidents? (hint: your table should be in wide format)
injury_count <- sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(county), !is.na(injury)) %>%
  filter(injury %in% c("none", "minor", "major", "fatal")) %>%
  count(county, injury) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = injury,
    values_from = n, 
    values_fill = 0
  )

  1. Use the table from #5 to make a plot that shows the total number of incidents by county.

  2. In the data, mode refers to a type of activity. Which activity is associated with the highest number of incidents?

sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(mode)) %>%
  count(mode, sort= TRUE)
## # A tibble: 8 × 2
##   mode                    n
##   <chr>               <int>
## 1 Surfing / Boarding     85
## 2 Freediving             36
## 3 Kayaking / Canoeing    30
## 4 Swimming               22
## 5 Scuba Diving           20
## 6 Hookah Diving          10
## 7 Paddleboarding          7
## 8 Walking in shallow      1
  1. Make a plot that compares the number of incidents by activity.
sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(mode)) %>%
  count(mode) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= reorder(mode, n), y= n)) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill=mode)) + 
  coord_flip() + 
  labs(
    title = "Number of Shark Incidents by Activity", x= "Activity", y= "Number of Incidents"
  )

  1. Which shark species is involved in the highest number of incidents?
sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(species)) %>%
  count(species, sort= TRUE)
## # A tibble: 11 × 2
##    species          n
##    <chr>        <int>
##  1 White          181
##  2 Hammerhead       3
##  3 Blue             2
##  4 Killer Whale     2
##  5 Leopard          2
##  6 Salmon           2
##  7 Blue*            1
##  8 Mako             1
##  9 Sevengill        1
## 10 Thresher         1
## 11 blue             1
  1. Are all incidents involving Great White’s fatal? Make a plot that shows the number and types of incidents for Great White’s only.
sharks %>%
  filter(!is.na(species), species== "White") %>%
  filter(!is.na(injury)) %>%
  count(injury) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x= reorder(injury,n), y=n)) + 
  geom_col(aes(fill=injury)) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(
    title = "Injuries for Great White Shark Incidents", x= "Type of Injury", y= "Number of Incidents"
  )
